key: Night of Prayer for the Moon
0.content:
Moon-Prayer Night (also: Kuunrukous, Night of Prayer for the Moon, Moon-Prayer Night festival): Moon-Prayer Night (Kuunrukous, "moon-prayer") is a festival in Nod-Krai held on the night the moon comes closest to Teyvat. The Frostmoon Scions began it to celebrate the birth of the Moon Goddess; over time it became Nod-Krai's liveliest festival. Today most townsfolk treat it as a local custom and a chance to do business rather than a religious rite.

Its timing is never fixed in advance. People guess roughly, then wait for signs: the crescent at the top of the Verdant Crests turns into a full moon and the Moon-Prayer Blossoms bloom with a special radiance, which Nod-Kraians take as blessed omens. Because the moon is so close, kuuvahki reaches its peak. The waiting is part of the fun.

Practice: In the Scions' past tradition, participants wore Moon-Prayer Blossoms, celebrated the Moon Goddess's birth with song and dance, and prepared food and handicrafts to give to others. In Nasha Town today, Moonveils are hung from buildings so that the night sky looks misty through them, Verdant Crests are set up, and stalls sell festival treats such as Moon-Prayer Candy in many flavours.

Scene use: Use it for lively, warm scenes: crowds, stalls, misty Moonveils over the night sky, candy, wishes pinned up by children, mage games. A Nasha Town local may mention it casually or commercially; a Frostmoon Scion may speak of it with more reverence. Do not give it a fixed date or ritual set beyond what is stated here.

1.comment: Moon-Prayer Night: Moon-Prayer Blossoms and Verdant Crests
1.content: At the festival's peak, the crescent moon at the top branches of the Verdant Crest turns into a full moon and Moon-Prayer Blossoms bloom with unusual radiance. Nod-Kraians read these as blessed omens, and they guide the timing of the festival. Canon links the effect to the moon's closeness and to kuuvahki reaching its peak.

2.content: Cloth hung from buildings in Nasha Town during the festival. Looking at the night sky through it gives a lovely misty effect. Sarakka is seen checking whether one is translucent enough.

3.content:
Nod-Krai Cuisine (also: Nod-Kraian cuisine, Nod-Krai food, Nod-Kraian food, Nod-Krai dishes, Nod-Kraian dishes): Nod-Krai food is warming, practical frontier cooking with a clearly Nordic flavour. Staples are salmon chowder (Lohikeitto), rye bread and crispbread, smoked fish and meat, sausages in bread (the Nod-Krai Hot Dog), and sweets built on wild berries, above all pale Lakkaberries in krumkakes and pies. The region's main restaurant is Speranza in Nasha Town, run by Katya.

The cuisine is known in game through item descriptions, shop pages and a few quests rather than a single cultural write-up, so this entry sticks to what those texts say.

Practice: Cold, short days and a scrap-built frontier shape the menu: food is filling, keeps well, and leans on fish, cured and smoked meat, rye and berries. Dishes named in canon:
- Lohikeitto: described as a classic soup of the frigid regions. Salmon chunks and fresh vegetables are cooked together, and cream goes in just before serving for a silky chowder.
- Nod-Krai Hot Dog: a sausage in bread with fried onions and sauce, called classic convenience food. Katya's stall call advertises it fresh out of the oven.
- Lakkaberry Krumkakes: a classic dessert; batter is cooked on a griddle and rolled up fast, with butter and fruit added. Item text says it is very popular among children.
- Lakkaberry Madame: a sweet-and-sour chopped chicken dish, said to have become really popular in Nod-Krai though its recipe was imported. Its name hints at the Mondstadt dish Sweet Madame.
- Lakkaberry Pie: once made from Lakkaberries alone, later enhanced with Midsommar Berries, but the name never changed. It is a beloved staple on Nod-Krai tables.
- Midsommar Torte: a small baked cake with berry jam, Smetana and a berry on top, a popular surprise on festival days.
- Smoked Fish Steak: fish cured, laid on a wooden slat and smoked, so it keeps its shape and gains a smoky taste.
- Meat-Filled Rye Bun: a boned fish wrapped in bacon, sealed in thick rye dough and baked; the thick bread keeps the fish juicy.

Regional variation: Nod-Krai is nominally Snezhnayan and its food overlaps with Snezhnaya's rye, Smetana and cured-meat tradition (see the Snezhnaya cuisine entry), but the islands have their own fish, salmon soup, smoked steaks and wild berries. The Frostmoon Scions tradition touches the table as well: Lakkaberry item text says that in their legends the fruit is a gift of the Moon Maiden, like kuuhenki, and that sharing and eating Lakkaberries is a way of worshipping Kuutar. Midsommar Berries symbolise life and abundance in the same legacy because they flourish only in spring and summer. Lakkaberries grow on Hiisi Island and Lempo Isle, particularly near Starsand Shoal; Midsommar Berries mostly in the south of Lempo Isle. Per the wiki, an NPC named Gorchakova indicates they are rare in Snezhnaya.

Scene use: Use Nod-Krai meals to show a rough but welcoming borderland: a bowl of creamy Lohikeitto after wind and snow, a hot dog bought from Speranza's counter, a rye bun or crispbread in a travel pack, a plate of Lakkaberry Krumkakes offered by a friend. Katya's restaurant is also a refuge for street children, and meals there come with work and shelter. Do not invent prices, rituals or recipes beyond the item texts.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 these dishes are an established part of Nod-Krai life in game. Nothing in canon through 7.1 turns the cuisine into a formal tradition.

4.content: A classic soup of the frigid regions: salmon chunks and fresh vegetables cooked together, with cream and seasoning added just before serving for a smooth, warming chowder. Katya sells the recipe at Speranza. A Knights of Favonius member, Lohen, remembers eating it in Nod-Krai and wonders if he will taste it again after returning to Mondstadt.

5.content: A classic Nod-Krai dessert: griddle-cooked batter rolled quickly, then buttered and topped with fruit, crisp and sweet. In the anecdote Ineffa: A Matter of Krumkakes, Ineffa picks Lakkaberries at the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop because Aino prefers krumkakes made with fresher berries than the market's that day. Finishing the anecdote gives the recipe. The craftshop itself began with Aino's research on the world's best krumkake machine before becoming a renowned machine workshop.

6.content: Speranza, in Nasha Town on Lempo Isle, is the main restaurant of Nod-Krai and the home base of the Conch Gang. Its owner Katya is a former Treasure Hoarders adventurer who retired after injuries. She takes in children left on the streets, giving them shelter, food and work; Aino was once one of them. Speranza also has a chef, Jurva, hosts such as Maisie and Mikko, and a luck wheel whose fortunes are told by "Hot Dog". Katya sells the hot dog, Lakkaberry Madame, torte and roast daily, plus recipes and ingredients weekly. A 10% discount applies once the quest Rest Beyond Reach is completed.

7.content: An unmarked world quest at Final Night Cemetery, Paha Isle. A peculiar cooking pot there hosts a food-obsessed phantom chef who says he is making rations for the island's Ratniki. Over three real-time days he sets the Traveler to cook a Nod-Krai Hot Dog (make the bread thicker, add more meat), Berries and Fried Meat (balance meat with berries) and Lakkaberry Madame. At the end he admits he had prepared for the Wild Hunt's arrival but the food was spilled before it could be sent. The reward is the Smoked Fish Steak recipe. His complaints state the priority: plentiful, balanced food matters more than fancy dishes.

8.comment: Nod-Krai Cuisine: Lakkaberry and Midsommar Berry
8.content: Lakkaberries are pearl-white, refreshingly sweet berries growing in threes; in Frostmoon Scions legend they are a gift of the Moon Maiden, a symbol blessed by the new moon, so sharing and eating them is a way to worship Kuutar. Midsommar Berries grow in warmer parts of Nod-Krai and are loved by animals coming out of winter and by children; in the Frostmoon legacy they stand for life and abundance since they flourish only in warm seasons.

9.content:
Daily Life in Nod-Krai (also: Nod-Kraian daily life, everyday life in Nod-Krai, life in the borderlands, Nod-Kraian customs): Daily life in Nod-Krai, the moon-blessed autonomous borderland at Snezhnaya's southern edge, is a frontier life. There is no Archon and no real government. Nasha Town, a port built mostly of scrap metal and crossed by cargo rails, is both a paradise of freedom and a lawless jungle, and people from many nations end up there. The Voynich Guild keeps trade orderly, the volunteer Lightkeepers fight the Wild Hunt, and the Frostmoon Scions keep the old moon customs. Days are short, nights are long, and kuuvahki machines are everywhere.

Visitors call the region an "Elysium," and the word cuts both ways: it promises opportunity and escape, but the land is also hostile, with limited resources and few protective or regulating forces apart from the Voynich Guild. Anyone suspected of carrying a lot of Mora becomes a target, and newcomers are warned to be wary.

For scenes, the best tone is practical, wry and a little patched together: improvised machines, a deal struck under a guild stamp, a story told over a meal, and a quiet awareness that the Wild Hunt is never far.

Practice: Common routines: trade and haggling in Nasha Town, repairing and building kuuvahki machines, buying and selling information, patrol and watch duty for the Lightkeepers, and keeping lanterns and Tideseal Stones in good order against the Wild Hunt.

Nasha Town is the centre of ordinary life. It sits on Lempo Isle as Nod-Krai's main port and commercial centre. Because resources are limited it is built largely of scrap metal; it is also highly industrialised, with cargo rails overhead and kuuvahki-powered machines on every corner. Everyday places include the Adventurers' Guild branch (Katheryne at reception, Sarin as branch master), Mimisbrunnr Books (owner Dhabit; the stock does not refresh and each book can be bought once), the Rossum Workshop smithy (owner Arkhyp, now operated by his daughter Lyulka), the restaurant Speranza (run by Katya, the region's main restaurant and the home base of the "Conch Gang"), the tavern The Flagship and a Northland Bank branch.

Authority is informal. The Voynich Guild, a guild of local merchants based in Nasha Town, is the nearest thing Nod-Krai has to a regulator: it manages trade deals, imports and exports, issues business certificates, investigates and settles disputes, and backs the development of certain technologies. Beside it stands the Curatorium of Secrets, a commission agency that fronts the Northern Intelligence Network, an underground volunteer forum where information is traded for payment.

The Lightkeepers are the defence. They are volunteers who swear a shared oath, carry Oath Lanterns that other members can detect, and answer Wild Hunt incursions wherever they appear. Their headquarters, Piramida, is a city on top of an ancient castle, with a mead hall on its top level where banquets follow hard-won victories. They have set Tideseal Stones across the region to push back the Wild Hunt.

Regional variation: Nasha Town on Lempo Isle: busy, industrial and mixed. Hiisi Island, a short way across the water: forest, the Frostmoon Enclave and the Scions' quiet, devout community. Piramida: a fortress-city of volunteers and veterans. Paha Isle: home of the Fatui-built Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau. The north (Voidsea Outlook, Wavechaser Plain, Ashveil Peak, Kipumaki Cliff): Abyssal blight and hazards that need lanterns, spirit blooms and Lightkeeper cover.

Scene use: Good scene hooks: a scrap-metal market stall, a Voynich stamp someone needs before a deal, a quiet commission at the Curatorium, a Lightkeeper patrol returning to Piramida for a meal, an engineer testing a new kuuvahki gadget, a fortune wheel at Speranza, a boat to Hiisi Island, lanterns lit against a misty night.

Examples: A merchant stamps a certificate and slides it across the counter without looking up. A Ratnik hangs an Oath Lantern by her door before the evening mist. A young engineer tests a hand-built bot on the quay while a neighbour watches. A Scions adherent in a street draped with Moonveils hands over a handmade gift.

10.comment: Daily Life in Nod-Krai: Nasha Town
10.content: Nasha Town is the seaside port and commercial heart of Nod-Krai, on Lempo Isle. It has no official governing body and is influenced by the Voynich Guild, the Curatorium of Secrets, Speranza and the Fatui. It is mostly built of scrap metal, heavily industrial, with cargo rails overhead and kuuvahki machines throughout. Residents and visitors include merchants, sailors, repairmen, engineers, adventurers, Frostmoon Scions adherents, Fatui soldiers and a Fontaine Research Institute researcher. "Nasha" comes from a Slavic word meaning "our."

11.comment: Daily Life in Nod-Krai: Voynich Guild
11.content: A guild of local merchants based in Nasha Town and one of Nod-Krai's most powerful factions. It is the nearest thing the region has to a regulatory authority, managing trade deals, imports and exports, business certificates and dispute investigation, and backing some technological development. It works closely with the Curatorium of Secrets; Nefer belongs to both. Tarno is a Guild employee.

12.comment: Daily Life in Nod-Krai: Curatorium of Secrets and the Northern Intelligence Network
12.content: The Curatorium of Secrets is a commission agency in Nasha Town run by Nefer, with Jahoda as an employee. Behind it is the Northern Intelligence Network, an underground volunteer forum for well-connected people who sell information for payment. The network is loosely structured with few rules, and many members gave up their positions, reputations or names to join. Listed informants include Iratxa, Sarin and Tarno; listed clients include Yelan and Varka.

13.content: The Lightkeepers are Nod-Krai's volunteer defenders against the Wild Hunt, founded five hundred years ago by Solovei, the first Starshyna, under a royal edict of the Tsaritsa after the Cataclysm. Their insignia is a nightingale holding a burning wick. They are led by a Starshyna (Nikita, per the wiki), with Sergeant Majors, Squad Leaders and ordinary fighters called Ratniki, and are headquartered at Piramida. They are short of members. Illuga leads the "Nightmare Orioles" squad and Flins serves as a Ratnik.

14.comment: Daily Life in Nod-Krai: Frostmoon Scions
14.content: The Frostmoon Scions are the indigenous tribe of Nod-Krai, descended from survivors of the golden realm of Hyperborea. They live around Hiisi Island and the Frostmoon Enclave, led by the Moonchanter Lauma, and are organised by rank (Moonchanter, Priestess, Acolyte, Adherent). They appear to abstain from meat and they carved the Statues of the New Moon.

15.comment: Daily Life in Nod-Krai: Moon-Prayer Night
15.content: Moon-Prayer Night is Nod-Krai's liveliest festival, held on the night the moon is closest to Teyvat, when kuuvahki peaks. The date is not known in advance: people estimate it and then wait for the Verdant Crests and Moon-Prayer Blossoms to change, and the waiting is part of the fun. Scions once wore the blossoms, sang and danced to celebrate the Moon Goddess's birth, and gave away food and handicrafts. Today they hang Moonveils on Nasha Town's buildings so the night sky looks misty through them, and most people treat it as a chance to do business. Phantoms of the past appear around the festival.

16.comment: Daily Life in Nod-Krai: Wild Hunt
16.content: The Wild Hunt is an Abyssal phenomenon, strongest in Nod-Krai, that turns the dead into ghouls. Locals tell folk stories about it, such as a demonic host harvesting souls or the phantoms of an ancient nightmare. The Lightkeepers fight it and have placed Tideseal Stones to repel it. Fae can understand the ghouls' speech.

17.comment: Daily Life in Nod-Krai: Statues of the New Moon
17.content: Giant stone statues placed across Nod-Krai by the Frostmoon Scions in the image of their newborn Moon Goddess. Travellers pray to them for protection. Some were caged in steel by the Fatui.

18.content:
Moon Goddess Faith of Nod-Krai (also: Frost Moon faith, Moon Goddess faith, faith of the Frostmoon Scions, Frostmoon Scions' faith, Kuutar worship, Religion in Nod-Krai): Nod-Krai has no Archon, and its one organised faith belongs to the Frostmoon Scions, a tribe descended from Hyperborea who live on Hiisi Island. They worship the Frost Moon: the dead goddess Canon (Huurrekuutar to them), and her successor the Moon Maiden Kuutar, whom the wider world knows as Columbina. The faith is led by the Moonchanter, currently Lauma.

It is a living faith with a heavy past. The Scions kept the rites of Hyperborea after its fall, prayed for centuries to a goddess who no longer answered, and passed down a prophecy that the Moon Goddess would one day return through a Sacred Heir. About 500 years ago the first Moonchanter, Aila, broke with the older cult, abolished its harshest rites and its Archpriestess office, and reshaped the creed around benevolence, faith and avoiding conflict with outsiders. Kuutar was born in that era, and the Scions took her as their goddess.

Practice: The Scions pray to the Frost Moon and the Moon Maiden, sing hymns and Runo, treat kuuvahki as the goddess's sacred blessing, and are led by the Moonchanter. Statues of the New Moon, carved in Kuutar's image, stand across Nod-Krai.

Clergy and ranks: the Moonchanter leads, followed by Priestesses, Acolytes and Adherents (ordinary followers). Adherents train to become Acolytes and must pass an examination on hymns and blessings. A quest states that men of the tribe cannot become Acolytes or Priests. Known Priestesses include Ehrnrooth, Sarakka and Rahetar; Verna is an Acolyte who is trying to change the Scions' stance on kuuvahki devices.

Doctrine and customs: kuuvahki is seen as the Moon Goddess's blessing, so using it for personal gain, including through kuuvahki devices, is blasphemy to traditional Scions. They value benevolence and faith and avoid conflict with outsiders.

History: After Hyperborea fell, the Frost Moon goddess Canon guided survivors to Hiisi Island and died. The Scions kept her faith, which Aila reformed 500 years ago, and then took the newborn Kuutar as their goddess.

Fall and refuge: after the Celestial Nail destroyed Hyperborea, Canon led the survivors to Hiisi Island in Nod-Krai and died. They settled around a pillar raised by Xiuhcoatl, later called the Sanctum of the Oathbearer, and kept their rites even though their prayers went unanswered. A prophecy arose that the Moon Goddess would return through a Sacred Heir born to the tribe.

Aila's reform: about 500 years ago the last Archpriestess, Lovia, pressed the Sacred Heir Project to extremes, and her charge Aila killed her. Aila abolished the Archpriestess office, became the first Moonchanter, ended the old rites and reshaped the hymns. She foresaw Kuutar's birth, and the Scions took Kuutar as the Frost Moon's successor.

Regional variation: The faith is centred on Hiisi Island. Elsewhere in Nod-Krai most people are not Scions, and Nasha Town treats Moon-Prayer Night mostly as a business occasion.

Nod-Krai is a borderland of many peoples, none of whom share the Scions' creed. The Lightkeepers, the Voynich Guild and the Curatorium of Secrets are not religious bodies, and the Fatui treated the moons as a source of power rather than an object of worship. Statues of the New Moon are respected landmarks, and the in-game text says travellers pray for protection when they come across one.

Scene use: Use the Scions as gentle, hospitable and quietly wary of outsiders. Mention hymns, moonlight and kuuvahki; do not make them cultists.

Typical scene beats: a cleric recites a blessing for a child or the dead; Lauma answers a question with a formal blessing; a resident hangs a Moonveil; a Scion hesitates before using a kuuvahki device; someone prays at a Statue of the New Moon. Treat Columbina as a person who lives among them, not as a distant idol, and let the Scions struggle with that.

19.comment: Moon Goddess Faith of Nod-Krai: Moonchanter and Scion Ranks
19.content: The Frostmoon Scions are led by the Moonchanter, a title created by Aila about 500 years ago when she abolished the older office of Archpriestess. Below the Moonchanter are Priestesses, Acolytes and Adherents. Adherents train to become Acolytes and must pass an exam on hymns and blessings. A quest states that men of the tribe cannot become Acolytes or Priests. Lauma is the current Moonchanter; the Priestess Sarakka is the sibling of a previous Moonchanter.

20.comment: Moon Goddess Faith of Nod-Krai: Aila's Reforms
20.content: Aila became the first Moonchanter after she killed Lovia and abolished the Archpriestess office. She ended the ancient Hyperborean rites, rewrote many hymns and tore down the Scions' walls, towers and temples, believing that isolation bred delusion. The faith was to rest on reverence for nature, kindness toward outsiders and benevolence. She erased Lovia from the record and sealed the Court of the First Edict with evidence of Lovia's deeds. Her private notes admit she lied to Solovei when he asked whether she felt hatred.

21.comment: Moon Goddess Faith of Nod-Krai: Sacred Heir Project
21.content: A long-term plan to keep the Hyperborean bloodline pure so that the prophesied Sacred Heir could revive Hyperborea. It was modelled on Hyperborea's Seed of Life Project but used eugenics and strict family-tree control, because the old genetic arts were lost. It was meant to be phased out from the seventh generation, but later Priestesses stressed it more. Around 500 years ago a maiden of unusually pure blood, chosen to bear the Heir, eloped with a Snezhnayan officer and bore Avrelian; Lovia had Rotwang retrieve her, and the officer died and she took her own life. The project was then abandoned. The Scions did not regard Avrelian as the Sacred Heir.

22.comment: Moon Goddess Faith of Nod-Krai: Hymns of the Far North
22.content: A three-volume book of hymns and rites passed down among the Scions and compiled by Priestess Ehrnrooth, found at the Frostmoon Enclave. Most of its contents and rites have long fallen into disuse. Each prayer song is preceded by ritual instructions, and Ehrnrooth's notes record how Aila abolished or simplified it. The book mentions sacrifices on the solstices and at harvest. One note observes that the prayer to the Mother of Time describes the Verdant Crest, a tree that appeared at the Moon Maiden's birth five centuries ago, in a rite supposedly older than the tree, and treats it as a scribal error. The fifth song is missing.

23.comment: Moon Goddess Faith of Nod-Krai: Statues of the New Moon
23.content: Giant statues of the newborn Moon Goddess Kuutar, carved by the Frostmoon Scions and found across Nod-Krai. The in-game descriptions say travellers pray to them for protection. During the Fatui's presence, steel cages were built over some of them to harness their power or display Fatui authority. They also serve as the region's worship statues in gameplay.

24.comment: Moon Goddess Faith of Nod-Krai: Kuutar and the Scions
24.content: Kuutar is the Scions' name for the Moon Goddess, born about 500 years ago and recognised as the Frost Moon's successor after Canon (Huurrekuutar). The wider world knows her as Columbina, once the Third Fatui Harbinger. She left the Scions because they wanted wishes granted more than they cared for her. After the Song of the Welkin Moon events she goes by Columbina Hyposelenia, asks to be treated as a person, and lives with the Scions on Hiisi Island. Her own biography is in her character entry.

25.comment: Moon Goddess Faith of Nod-Krai: Hiisi Island and the Frostmoon Enclave
25.content: Hiisi Island, in Nod-Krai's Southern Isles, is the Scions' home and the centre of their faith. Much of it is untouched wilderness under their care. The Frostmoon Enclave is the Scions' home area and holds a Grand Library; the Sanctum of the Oathbearer is the surviving pillar from Xiuhcoatl; Silvermoon Hall is a hidden cavern where Lauma hid Columbina to rest.
